data.name: PP242
data.description: An ATP-competitive mTOR kinase inhibitor (a 'TORKinib'); like Torin1, inhibits both mTORC1 and mTORC2 and blocks outputs that rapamycin leaves intact.
data.description_beginner: A lab tool drug, similar to Torin1, that blocks mTOR's active site directly. Like Torin1, it shuts down both mTOR complexes, unlike rapamycin which mainly hits one.

studies.title: Active-site inhibitors of mTOR target rapamycin-resistant outputs of mTORC1 and mTORC2
studies.authors: Feldman ME; Apsel B; Uotila A; Loewith R; Knight ZA; Ruggero D; Shokat KM

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: The parallel discovery to Thoreen 2009 (same year), from the Shokat lab. Their TORKinibs (PP242, PP30) block mTOR's active site, hitting both complexes and shutting down cap-dependent translation that rapamycin misses. Together these two papers established a whole new drug class beyond rapamycin.

studies.title: Effective and selective targeting of leukemia cells using a TORC1/2 kinase inhibitor
studies.authors: Janes MR; Limon JJ; So L; Chen J; Lim RJ; Chavez MA; Vu C; Lilly MB; Mallya S; Ong ST; Konopleva M; Martin MB; Ren P; Liu Y; Rommel C; Fruman DA

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: The ATP-competitive TORC1/2 inhibitor PP242 selectively kills leukemia cells, with much weaker effects on the proliferation and function of normal lymphocytes.

studies.title: Distinct perturbation of the translatome by the antidiabetic drug metformin
studies.authors: Larsson O; Morita M; Topisirovic I; Alain T; Blouin MJ; Pollak M; Sonenberg N

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Human cancer cell line (per MeSH); genome-wide polysome microarray translatome analysis comparing metformin, rapamycin and PP242
studies.finding: The authors compared genome-wide changes in mRNA translation caused by metformin with those caused by the mTOR inhibitors rapamycin and PP242 in cancer cells. Metformin changed gene expression at the level of translation to an extent comparable to the classic mTOR inhibitors. Its antiproliferative effect could be explained by selective suppression of translation of mRNAs encoding cell-cycle regulators, acting through the mTORC1 / 4E-BP pathway. The paper provided evidence that metformin's effect on cell growth in vitro goes through selective translational control rather than a general drop in protein synthesis. Boundary: Cultured cancer cells at drug concentrations used in vitro; does not show that metformin at clinical doses acts this way in patients. Drafted from the abstract only.
